preamble: Monophthongization of 'ei' to 'i' involves the simplification of the diphthong into a single high front vowel, common in Germanic languages including English.

examples.note: Historical monophthongization where diphthongs simplify to high front vowels.

languageExamples.language: Ancient Greek to Koine / Modern Greek

examples.note: Classical ει (by then [eː]) raised to [i] by the Roman period; η followed later

sources: Ladefoged, P. (2001). A Course in Phonetics.
Alkire, T., & Rosen, C. (2010). Romance Languages: A Historical Introduction. Cambridge University Press.
Allen, W. S. (1987). Vox Graeca: The Pronunciation of Classical Greek. 3rd ed. Cambridge University Press.
